Explain why probabilities of equally likely outcomes can be found by counting.
items.answer: If all n outcomes are equally likely, each has probability 1/n, so an event containing k outcomes has probability k/n.

items.stem:
Let f(x) = (1 + 2x)/(1 − x).
(a) Expand (1 − x)⁻¹ as far as the term in x³.
(b) Hence find the expansion of (1 + 2x)/(1 − x) up to the term in x³.
(c) State the range of values of x for which the expansion is valid.
(d) Use your expansion with x = 1/10 to estimate 4/3 as a decimal.
(e) Explain why x = 1/2 would not give a reliable estimate.
items.answer: (a) 1 + x + x² + x³ (b) 1 + 3x + 3x² + 3x³ (c) |x| < 1 (d) 1.333000 (e) convergence is slow; many terms needed

Isabel has CHF 10000 to invest. Option A pays 4.5% per annum compounded annually. Option B pays 4.3% per annum compounded quarterly.
(a) Find the value of Option A after 5 years.
(b) Find the value of Option B after 5 years.
(c) State which option is better, giving a reason.
(d) Inflation is 2% per year. Find the real value, in today's money, of the better option after 5 years.
items.answer: (a) CHF 12,461.82 (b) CHF 12,384.40 (c) Option A: larger final value (d) CHF 11,287.05

items.stem:
A small data set is given: 36, 39, 40, 54, 56, 57, 60, 61, 61, 65, 68, 104.
(a) State whether the data are discrete or continuous.
(b) Find the median and interquartile range.
(c) Show that 104 is an outlier.
(d) Find the mean with and without the outlier.
(e) Explain which measure of centre is more appropriate for these data.
items.answer: (a) discrete (b) 58.5; 16 (c) 104 > Q3 + 1.5 × IQR = 87 (d) 58.4; 54.3 (e) the median, as it is not affected by the outlier

items.stem:
This question develops a formula for the variance.
(a) Show that Σ(xᵢ − x̄)² = Σxᵢ² − n x̄².
(b) Hence show that σ² = (Σx²)/n − x̄².
(c) For the data 1, 2, …, 7, find the mean and the variance in exact form.
(d) Prove that, for the first n positive integers, σ² = (n² − 1)/12.
(e) Deduce the variance of the values a + d, a + 2d, …, a + nd.
items.answer: (a) proof (b) divide by n (c) 4; 4 (d) proof (e) d²(n² − 1)/12

items.stem:
In this question give exact answers where possible.
(a) Solve e^(2x) = 2eˣ, giving your answer in exact form.
(b) Explain why the solution in (a) is the only one.
(c) Solve e^(2x) − 4eˣ + 4 = 0.
(d) Use your GDC to solve e^(2x) = 4eˣ − x.
(e) Explain why an analytic method cannot be used for the equation in (d).
items.answer: (a) x = ln 2 (b) eˣ ≠ 0, so dividing by eˣ loses no solution (c) x = ln 2 (d) 1.29 (e) the equation mixes eˣ and x terms; no algebraic rearrangement isolates x
